To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the data source selection method based on clustering outperforms all other methods, (ii) progressive stepwise data exchanges improve performance, and (iii) the performance of the progressive stepwise data source selection is not significantly affected by load balancing.

(a) a clustering-based data source selection method is the best method to select the data sources that are most likely contribute to the query results, (b) the data source selection method that uses the best peer ranking scheme is the one that uses the cosine similarity measure to rank peers, and (c) the data exchange methods that use a stepwise approach to update each peer's summary are the best methods to improve the system's query performance.
the data exchange methods improve the performance of the data source selection approach and that the load balancing is improved by the data exchange methods.

the problem of similarity search in P2P networks.
data source selection for content-based image retrieval in peer-to-peer networks, where peers are clustered according to their image content and the load of the clusters is balanced.
the development of a load balanced, scalable data source selection approach for P2P networks that supports high-dimensional vector data.

the data exchange methods improve the system performance, especially for high-dimensional queries.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new method for similarity search in P2P networks, which is based on a clustering-based data source selection approach.
we present a data source selection algorithm that is based on clustering, and which is able to deal with high-dimensional data, and which is load-balancing.
we present two methods to improve data source selection for content-based image retrieval (CBIR), which is one of the most important application areas of P2P networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed progressive data exchange methods can be used to improve the performance of data source selection approaches.
data source selection methods are a promising alternative to the traditional approach of contacting all peers in the network when processing similarity queries.
data exchange between peers is a promising approach to improve the system's efficiency, especially in the presence of skewed data distributions.
